subject: Network topology brief & migration runbook for SOC 2 / SIG review
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: BrightScale Security <security@brightscale.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Network topology brief & migration runbook for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi team —

Thanks again for taking a look at our control plane and private deployment boundaries as part of BrightScale's SOC 2 / SIG intake. Attached is a concise topology brief (network-diagram-v2.png) and a proposed migration/runbook workbook (migration-checklist-20261102.xlsx) that maps the steps we intend to follow if you want to onboard Redwood Private (VPC deployment) into your compliance scope. I also attached the current segmentation-matrix.csv for quick reference.

High level notes:
- The redwood-private VPC is logically separated from hosted control plane traffic; control-plane egress is restricted to a limited set of management IPs and TLS-only endpoints.
- Customer workloads run in their tenant-enclaves (dedicated projects) with per-tenant KV cache isolation.
- KMS boundary: customer data keys are stored in a customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; we hold wrapping keys only with strict ACLs for Dedicated reservations.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the attached level of detail is sufficient for your SIG review? If not, which diagrams or callouts would you like expanded (e.g., flow-level egress arrows, service account mapping, or subnet IDs)?
2) Would you prefer a live walkthrough of the diagram or a short recorded demo (20–30m)?

Proposed times: Tue/Wed 11/3–11/4 between 10–12 PT — happy to adjust to your availability.

Thanks — attaching the files and a link to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xA_briefing_network_topology_2026

Best,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: network-diagram-v2.png (image/png), migration-checklist-20261102.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), segmentation-matrix.csv (text/csv)

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 12:01:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Network topology brief & migration runbook for SOC 2 / SIG review

David —

Appreciate the materials, this is a great start. Two quick clarifying questions before we schedule a walkthrough:

1) Egress & observability: the diagram shows a control-plane egress ACL to a set of management endpoints. Can you enumerate the exact FQDNs/IP ranges you expect to be permitted during a migration window? We need these for our firewall zoning and to validate outbound control-plane telemetry retention.

2) KMS / key custody model: you noted customer-managed KMS for Private. For Dedicated (reserved capacity), do you also support customer-managed keys? If not, what encryption-at-rest assurances and key custodian audit logs can you provide?

If you can answer in-thread we can determine whether a short demo suffices or whether we need a full SIG whiteboard session.

Thanks,

—BrightScale Security
Heather Lane
Security & Compliance Manager
BrightScale Inc.
security@brightscale.com

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Network topology brief & migration runbook for SOC 2 / SIG review

Heather / team —

Thanks for the rapid review. Answers inline below and I’ve attached a short control-plane egress matrix (controlplane-egress-matrix.pdf) with the canonical FQDNs/IP blocks we recommend during onboarding windows. Quick summary:

1) Egress & observability: permitted endpoints during migration/walkthrough:
   - telemetry.redwood.ai (443) — 34.210.112.0/24, 52.23.44.0/24 (TLS only)
   - rpm-api.redwood.ai (443) — 34.211.128.0/24
   - kms-ops.redwood.ai (443) — traffic to/from customer KMS proxy (see matrix)
   Note: we publish a CIDR allowlist in the shared drive and we can provide a signed manifest for your ingress firewall team.

2) KMS / key custody:
   - Private (customer VPC): we support full customer-managed KMS where customers bring their own keys (BYOK) and we only see wrapped material; we provide HSM-backed attestations on request.
   - Dedicated (reserved): we support both options — customers can choose BYOK (via a managed KMS proxy) or Redwood-managed wrapping keys. If Redwood-managed, we provide monthly key-rotation logs, KMS access audit trails, and the ability to generate exportable key usage reports for your auditors.

Additional notes:
- Retention: telemetry and API request logs used for debugging are retained in an access-controlled bucket for 90 days by default; longer retention can be arranged under contract.
- Network flows: the attached PDF includes an expanded control-plane-to-tenant flow and shows the egress proxy / TLS inspection hop we use for non-customer-managed KMS scenarios.

Demo preference: a 25-minute live walkthrough tomorrow (11/4) at 10:30 PT works for our engineering lead (Marissa). If that time is tight for you, we can send a 12-minute recorded walkthrough instead.

Link to updated artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xA_briefing_network_topology_2026

Thanks,
David
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
Attachment stub: controlplane-egress-matrix.pdf (application/pdf)
